docs.task: How explore tasks are created and run, and how research documents are stored per session.

asks: How research documents are stored per session

data_flow.step: A session is created. The runner makes `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<session id>/`, writes `sessions/.gitignore` (`*`) once, and creates one subfolder per project in the session. It appends `SessionCreated` carrying `session_root`; the fold copies it into `SessionState.session_root`. The row goes to the `sessions` table and every event to the `events` table of `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.db`.

The planner finds no category and pushes `Step::Judge { Classify }`. The Classify decision is folded by `apply_classify`: for Research, Spec, Plan and Implement it drops earlier Classify-origin tasks and calls `push_explore(project, task, ExploreOrigin::Classify)` for each valid `explore_tasks` entry. When the judge returned none, it makes one task per project in scope with the full request as text (Rule D1).

Later tasks come from other events: the Sufficiency judge (up to `MAX_SUFFICIENCY_RESEARCH = 3` per round, `SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS = 3` rounds, duplicates of an unfinished same-project same-text task skipped); `Amended` context (Amendment origin, for Research, Spec, Plan, Implement); the Route answer / Feedback judges through `queue_research` (up to `MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH = 3`); the Rescue judge's `Explore` action (Rescue origin, loop-bound); and an `AgentAsked` event whose target is `agent: explore` (Ask origin, loop-bound).

`next_steps` runs `flows`, which calls `explore_tasks` for every category before the category match. Each unstarted, non-abandoned, non-failed task becomes a `Step::Spawn` with `ExecPurpose::Explore { task: idx }`, `project`, and `session_dir = project_session_dir(project)` (`<session root>/<project key>`). The task text is `t.task` plus `added_context()`.
The driver loop in the runner inserts `step.key()` into `inflight` and spawns a tokio task per step; a key already in flight is skipped. `perform` routes `Step::Spawn` to `perform_spawn`.

`perform_spawn` acquires an execution slot (`limits.max_parallel_executions`), returns early for a terminal or paused session, and returns early for a task already marked abandoned while the spawn waited for a slot (Rule U1). It resolves the route for agent key `explore` (default tier advanced), loads the project's profile and inventory, creates `req.session_dir`, and calls `factory.build`, which fills `ExploreParams { common, task, extra: Extras::default() }`. The rendered block has `Task:`, `Workspace root:`, `Repo root:`, `Session dir:` and `Repo key:`.

The runner appends `ExecutionStarted` (agent, purpose, stage, project, executor, model, params, spawn_block) and inserts a row in `executions`. The fold's `on_started` sets `task.exec`, `task.running = true`, `task.failed = None`. The executor (native or harness) then runs the agent with the `Document` capability, a `submit_explore` tool whose schema is `ExploreSubmit`, and a timeout of 1800 s.

The agent calls `Document` with `path = <session dir>/ostra-research-<YYYYMMDD-HHmmss>-<slug>.md`. The tool validates prefix, suffix and parent directory, parses the value as `ResearchDoc`, and `doc::write` stores `<name>.json` (pretty JSON source) and `<name>.md` (rendered). Direct Write/Edit of `ostra-research-*` is denied by the `ARTIFACTS` guard for every agent except explore, and the explore prompt tells it to use only `Document`.

The agent calls `submit_explore`. `check_submit` reads `research_path`, requires a loadable document with no error-level issues, and `validate_submit` checks the `ExploreSubmit` shape. A refused submit returns the problem to the agent so it can fix the document and submit again.

The runner stores the result in `executions.submit` and appends `ExecutionFinished`. `on_finished` sets `task.result = Some(sub)` on an OK submit; an Interrupted run clears `task.exec` so the task respawns; an Error with `retries < ERROR_RETRIES (1)` clears `exec` and increments `retries`; otherwise `task.failed` is set and the planner opens an execution-failed gate (except Ask origin). A Rescue-origin result also moves its loop to `Work` with the findings summary and `research_path` as the fact.

`explore_complete` returns true when every non-loop-bound task is finished, no finished task has an unjudged non-empty `not_covered` (otherwise it pushes a Sufficiency judge, up to 3 rounds), and `research_docs()` is non-empty. With no document in a Research, Spec, Plan or Implement session it pushes `Step::Fail` (Rule D1). The spec spawn receives `research_docs: s.research_docs()`; on a spec revision `new_research_docs` is the subset not yet in `applied.docs`.

The console reads documents through `/api/artifacts?path=`, which accepts only files inside a workspace's `sessions` root and attaches `ostra_core::doc::load_view(&path)` (typed document plus check issues) when the file name has a research, spec or plan prefix. The board lists each finished task's path as an `ArtifactRef` with kind `research` and the task's project.

patterns.description: Explore tasks are fold state. The pure planner walks `s.explore` and emits one `Step::Spawn` for each task with no execution yet that is neither abandoned nor failed. The step's `key()` is `spawn:` plus the serialized `ExecPurpose::Explore { task }`, so the runner's `inflight` set never starts a task twice. The spawn's `session_dir` is the project's folder under the session root, and the task text is the stored task plus any delivered added context. A failed task whose origin is not `Ask` opens an execution-failed gate; for `Ask` origin the failure is the asker's answer (Rule H3).
patterns.name: Planner emits a spawn per unstarted explore task

patterns.description: Every explore task is created by `SessionState::push_explore` while folding an event: the index is the current length of the `explore` vector, and `ExecPurpose::Explore { task }` carries that index. Callers are `apply_classify` (origin Classify), the Sufficiency judge decision (Sufficiency), `on_amended` (Amendment), `queue_research` (Answer, LoopAnswer, Amendment), the Rescue judge decision (Rescue), and the `AgentAsked` coordination event (Ask).
patterns.name: Task creation only inside the fold through push_explore

patterns.description: The fold stores no separate document registry. `research_docs()` maps each task's `ExploreSubmit.research_path` in task order. Spec receives this list as `Research docs:`; the session context file, the board artifact list, and several judge inputs read the same function or the same `result` field.
patterns.name: Research document list is derived from task results

patterns.description: The explore agent can only produce a research document through `Document`. The tool checks the `ostra-research-` prefix and `.md` suffix, then that the file's parent equals `ctx.session_dir` (the spawn's `Session dir:`, which for explore is `<session root>/<project key>`). Then `doc::write` stores `<name>.json` and renders `<name>.md`. The Layer 1 guard `ARTIFACTS` separately stops any other agent from writing those names.
patterns.name: Document tool confines a research file to the execution's session dir

patterns.description: Each explore rule has a fixture in `tests/conformance/main.rs` built with the `H` helper. Explore results are injected with `explore_submit(i, not_covered)`, whose `research_path` is `/ws/.ostra/sessions/s1/p/ostra-research-{i}.md`, matching the `<session root>/<project>/` layout.
patterns.name: Conformance fixture per explore rule

document.problem: Research is produced by explore executions that each write one typed research document. The questions are where an explore task comes from, what runs it, where its document lands on disk and in the event log, and how later stages find it. Nothing in the code reads research from an earlier session; every lookup is scoped to the current session's fold.
document.scope: Task: how explore tasks are created and run, and how research documents are stored per session. Covers the engine fold and planner, the spawn path, the Document tool and its guards, and the on-disk and database layout. It does not cover the judge prompts' wording, the harness executors' internals, or the web UI rendering of research documents.
document.title: Explore tasks and per-session research documents

submit.findings_summary: Explore tasks are fold state: SessionState::push_explore appends an ExploreTask (index = vector position) from Classify, Sufficiency, Amendment, Route answer/Feedback, Rescue, and agent-asked helper events. The pure planner's explore_tasks emits one Step::Spawn per unstarted task, and the runner's perform_spawn takes an execution slot, builds ExploreParams, and appends ExecutionStarted and ExecutionFinished. Each run's Session dir is `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<id>/<project key>/`. The Document tool accepts a file only directly in that dir, named `ostra-research-<stamp>-<slug>.md`, and writes a `.json` source plus a rendered `.md`. The session has no research registry: research_docs() maps each finished task's research_path, events and executions go to workspace.db, and nothing reads research from other sessions. docs/start/first-session.md says research sits at the session root, which the code contradicts; only spec and plan use the root.
not_covered: Judge prompt wording for Classify, Sufficiency, Route answer and Rescue (assets/judges/*.md)
Native and harness executor internals that enforce Document and submit ordering at run time
Restart recovery and handling of orphaned research files from interrupted or re-run tasks (crates/ostra-engine/tests/recover.rs)
Web console rendering of research documents and the separate workspace artifacts store (<workspace>/.ostra/artifacts/)
Whether web/ or the judge assets read research from other sessions; crates/ shows no such consumer
submit.scope_covered: How explore tasks are created and run, and how research documents are stored per session, in the engine fold and planner, the spawn path, the Document tool and guards, and the DB and disk layout; judge prompt wording, executor internals, restart recovery and web rendering were left out.

data_flow.step: An explore agent calls Document with path set to <session dir>/ostra-research-{run-stamp}-{slug}.md. The tool refuses any directory other than the calling session's Session dir.
doc::write validates the typed ResearchDoc, runs check, writes the .json sibling and renders the .md. No hash, commit id, or file fingerprint is stored.
The explore agent submits research_path, scope_covered, findings_summary, and not_covered. The fold stores the path on the explore task's result.
The Sufficiency judge, the Track judge, generate-spec, the light-track implementers, and the session context file all receive paths from that same session-only list (Rule D2, Rule F2).

When the session ends, the files stay under .ostra/sessions/<session-id>/. A later session's sandboxed shell and harness tools cannot see them because .ostra/sessions/ is hidden and only the running session is bound back. A native-executor Read is not refused by check_read, because the sessions folder is not in Roots.secret. The console can open any file in any session folder of the workspace.

A reader who has the earlier document's path (from the console, an upload, or a tagged artifact copy) reads the .md or its .json and judges currency with the facts it records: date, file paths, symbols, snippet sources, versions, lessons marked verified, and not_covered. The judgment is made against the current repo with Read, Grep, CodeOutline, CodeFind, and git in the shell.

patterns.description: Every stage after explore receives research documents as a list of paths built from the session's own explore results. A path from another session would have to be added to that list or typed into a task, because the fold only knows this session's explore tasks.

patterns.description: The documentation stage looks for a book written by an earlier session of the same project set and passes it as Existing book:. The lookup is a filesystem check at spawn time, so the fold stays a pure function of the log (CLAUDE.md pattern 1). Any reuse of research documents from another session would face the same constraint: the fact that it was reused must be recorded in an event if it changes how later events fold.

patterns.description: Rule B9 decides which parts of the earlier book to keep by comparing the areas the existing part records with the areas this session's changed files touch (module-map areas from INVENTORY.md). Untouched areas keep their sections. This is the repo's only logic that decides whether earlier agent output still applies, and it works at module-map-area granularity using the session's changed files.
patterns.name: Currency by touched areas, not by hash

patterns.description: Paths reach an agent as labeled lines in its first message. document.problem: A research document is written by the explore agent into one session's directory and is only ever handed to later stages of that same session. Nothing in the engine lists, searches, or injects research documents from another session. Reuse today therefore depends on a path reaching the new session some other way, and on the reader judging currency against the code, because the stored document carries no commit, hash, or per-file fingerprint.
document.scope: Task: how a session could find an earlier session's research documents and decide they still apply. Covers what Ostra does today in the Rust backend for locating, reading, and validating a research document that belongs to another session. It does not cover the web console, the harness adapters beyond the sandbox profile, or any design for a new feature. No external technology is involved, so no web sources were retrieved.
document.title: Reusing an earlier session's research documents

submit.findings_summary: Research documents are written by the Document tool into one session's folder under .ostra/sessions/<id>/ as a .md rendered from a .json sibling. The engine hands them only to later stages of the same session (SessionState::research_docs), so nothing lists or injects another session's documents. The sandbox hides other sessions from harness and shell executions, while the native read policy does not refuse that folder, so behavior differs by executor. The stored ResearchDoc has no commit, hash, or per-file fingerprint, so currency can only be judged against the current repo with Read, the code index, and git. The closest precedents are the cross-session documentation book (existing_book at spawn time, Rule B9 touched-areas check) and recalled memory lessons, which the explore prompt already tells agents to verify against current code.
not_covered: How the web console presents earlier sessions' artifacts and whether it can copy a research document path into a new task.
How the Classify judge and Route answer judge treat a path to an earlier research document in a request or an addition.
How git staging and commits relate to a session's run stamp, which would date a document's claims.
Harness executors' handling of a Read outside the sandbox profile, beyond the sandbox profile and the native policy.
submit.scope_covered: How a session could find an earlier session's research documents and decide they still apply, as the Rust backend does it today; the web console, harness adapters, and any design for a new feature were left out.
